main_text.p: feptentrionibus alluit, quâ Amasus, quâ Dullartus se sinuant, in orâ aggeribus perpetuis, opere difficillimo, sepitur & defenditur contra aquarum influxum: idemque, ut dixi jam ante, secundùm Hunesi lapsum fit non ab urbe solùm, sed & supra urbem, usque ad ejusdem ostium. In eâ post Groningam nobilissima & maxima DAMMONA est, non vilis oppidiDAMMONA. instar, si ambitum, & frequentiam habitatorum, si aedificiorum numerum, magnitudinem, formam, si viarum habitum spectes, sed honore moenium, & jure imperii civilis magistratuumque carens, amœna, in circulum ferè se colligens, fosaque utplurimùm cingens, templo illustri cum turre latè spectabili insignis; fanum quoque monasticum peramplum, sed extra ambitum, lateri tamen occiduo penè contiguum habens familiae Augustinianae, nunc ab omni cultu desertum, ac vix se sustinens: sita ad Fivelam amnem duobus infra Groningam milliaribus cæciam versùs, eodemque amne navigabili media divisa, pontibus intus connexa quinque; unde ad exitum

page.notes: Running head is printed as "Deque Vrbe Groninga."; the V is normalised to U. The page number "17" at the top right is read from a small scan and marked uncertain. Printed text is set in roman with long s; s is transcribed plainly. The section letter "B" and the catchword "amnis," sit at the foot. The initial word "feptentrionibus" begins the page as a fragment continuing from the previous page. The marginal note reads "DAMMONA." in small capitals, followed by a short dash-like mark.
